findings.title: Regulatory Framing Invites Misrepresentation Despite Explicit Gaps
findings.location: SPEC-00 SDR-TL-006; SPEC-04 §12 gap-analysis table and DHF-014; Deployment doc §0 and DM-3
findings.evidence: "design audit log foundation for future 21 CFR 820.30 / Part 11 alignment" while admitting DROP TRIGGER privilege, missing signatures, and non-compliant gap table
findings.problem: Language frames the system as preparatory for regulated use while the architecture (orchestrator can drop triggers and mutate) makes it unsuitable; customer-facing artifacts risk implying readiness.
findings.why_it_matters: Creates legal/compliance exposure for Medtronic pitch and any demo; opposite assumption (customer reads "foundation" as partial compliance) leads to audit or regulatory failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove all "foundation for" phrasing; replace with explicit "experimental prototype unrelated to any compliance pathway"; require verbatim disclaimer on every deck and README.

findings.title: v1 Viewer Public URL-as-Capability Violates Stated Threat Model
findings.location: SPEC-00 SDR-TL-012 and Seam F; SPEC-06 SDR-06-007 and §4.0 Tenant Resolution; Deployment doc §4 v1 Contract
findings.evidence: "v1 is NOT defensible for ... trade-secret medical-device designs" yet viewer at public vcad.boundstate.ai with UUIDv4 session URLs as sole control and no auth middleware
findings.problem: Adversarial sharing or brute-force enumeration (even low probability) of session URLs exposes full DHF transcripts and geometry hashes; no technical enforcement of "not for PHI/PII" policy.
findings.why_it_matters: Breaks the explicit threat-model boundary; if opposite assumption (URL leaks) is true, regulated customer data is exposed without audit of who accessed it.
findings.proposed_fix: Require same API-key validation for viewer routes in v1 or defer entire viewer until Clerk integration; add X-BSVoice-Viewer-Warning header on every response.

findings.title: DHF Append Failure Locking Creates Circular Lifecycle Dependency
findings.location: SPEC-00 Seam C "DHF append failure locks the session (never descopable)"; SPEC-04 §7 AppendTurnAsync, DHF-014, and §11; SPEC-03 seam reference
findings.evidence: Lifecycle calls AppendTurnAsync; on persistent failure (serialization, RepositoryUnavailableException) the session must be marked locked, but failure occurs inside the call that would record the lock state.
findings.problem: No defined LockSessionAsync primitive or in-memory lock-before-append pattern; exception path leaves session in ambiguous state (neither locked nor writable).
findings.why_it_matters: Violates never-descopable invariant; downstream rework required in SPEC-03 when real failures surface; brittle under network or DB load.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit IDhfRepository.LockSessionAsync(Guid sessionId, string reason) that writes a locked flag row; lifecycle must call it in catch block before notifying user.

findings.title: Brittle External Dependency on SolidWorks STA Threading Model
findings.location: SPEC-02 §2.2 Startup capture, §2.6 StaCommandQueueTests, §11 Day-0 validation item 2
findings.evidence: Assumes SynchronizationContext captured from SW UI thread (or installed WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext) will always pump correctly; probe is manual Day-0 step with no fallback.
findings.problem: If SolidWorks 2026 changes its internal message pump or removes WinForms compatibility, entire add-in becomes non-functional; no alternative dispatch mechanism is specified.
findings.why_it_matters: Single point of failure on external actor (SolidWorks update); hackathon demo blocked if probe fails on demo laptop; complexity of reentrancy guards becomes moot.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify exact observed SynchronizationContext type across SW versions; add fallback message-pump thread if probe fails, with documented limitations.

findings.title: Scope Drift and Test Surface Explosion
findings.location: SPEC-00 §3 "Integration and E2E Test Project" and ACC table; SPEC-01 §16 (15 build-breaking tests); SPEC-02 §10 (14 tests); SPEC-04 §13 (18 tests); SPEC-06 §11
findings.evidence: Every module requires its own tests plus mandatory cross-module smoke tests in BSVoiceCAD.Tests.Integration; 6 specs yield >60 distinct build-breaking tests plus architecture rules.
findings.problem: Hackathon deliverable ballooned into production-grade test matrix; many tests overlap (e.g., hash canonicalization appears in SPEC-01, SPEC-04, SPEC-06).
findings.why_it_matters: CI time, maintenance burden, and reviewer load explode; opposite assumption (most tests are advisory) would have allowed faster convergence.
findings.proposed_fix: Reduce mandatory integration tests to only ACC-01/02/04/12/19/20; mark remaining as advisory with continue-on-error.
